why: TWO STATES, AND BOTH EXIST BECAUSE THE OPEN-LOOP ARM IS UNREACHED BY THE
GENERATED CORPUS FOR A REASON THE CORPUS CANNOT FIX ITSELF. The first sweep
scored 47 of 58 and the eleven survivors partition into exactly two places:
the StC_Mode == 2 arm    lines 170, 172, 206, 207   7 survivors
the two ErrMsg helpers   lines 85, 112              4 survivors
Six of the seven at the open-loop arm were a DEFENSIVE GUARD this
translation had and the reference does not, and they were removed by
rewriting the gather rather than excused -- see the comment at that site.
The state below is what reaches the arm at all.
WHY THE ARM IS UNREACHED WITHOUT IT, and it is a conjunction of four
conditions no ladder crosses: `StC_Mode == 2` AND `StC_Group_N >= 1` AND
`Ind_StructControl(1) > 0` AND an `OL_StructControl` whose row contents
reach a compared output through `interp1d`. R6 crosses the FOUR quantities
this unit's own predicates test -- StC_Mode, StC_Group_N, aviFAIL and Time
-- at the full cross product, so `StC_Mode = 2` with `StC_Group_N = 1` IS
generated; what those cases do not have is `Ind_StructControl(1) > 0`, which
is not a predicate quantity of a knob shape (the subscript is the loop
counter, and the generator's own note says so: `CntrPar_Ind_StructControl
[I_GROUP - 1]: subscript not traceable to a parameter`).
`Ind_StructControl` IS A RAMP FROM 1, NOT FROM 5, and the 1 is the point:
the survivor at line 172 is `Ind_StructControl(I_GROUP) > 0` widened to
`> 1`, which changes an answer only where the index is EXACTLY 1. R5's
array-elements-distinct rule is observed by the step -- unit #38 measured
what a constant ramp costs, and unit #29 before it.
`OL_Breakpoints` IS STRICTLY INCREASING BECAUSE `interp1d` CHECKS IT.
The callee sets `aviFAIL = -1` and writes a message when its xData is not
strictly increasing, which is an admissible input for the reference but not
an admissible BASELINE: R11's whole property is that exactly one predicate
is away from admissible in each case, and a baseline that entered the error
path would put a second one there in every case built from it.
`LocalVar_Time` IS 1.5, INSIDE THE BREAKPOINTS, so the interpolation runs
its interior arm and every element of the gathered row can reach the answer
-- which is what the two loop-shape survivors at lines 206/207 need. Time is
also one of the four knobs, so R11 moves it to 0, 1, 2, 499, 500 and 501
from this state, and the 499/500/501 rungs put the `Time > 500` step of the
OTHER arm under the same state's other knob values.
`CntrPar_StC_GroupIndex` IS A RAMP FROM 1 rather than the shipped 2801,
because `harness/ranges.toml` pins it to 1..3000 and the ramp keeps the
elements distinct: with every group index equal, the copy loop's
`StC_GroupIndex(I_GROUP)` and `StC_GroupIndex(1)` write the same avrSWAP
slot and an index shift there is unkillable. It is 1-based and the array is
3000 long, so `I_GROUP` up to `StC_Group_N` (pinned at 3) stays in range.
STATE 2 IS THE ERROR PATH AND IT IS A SEPARATE STATE FOR R11's OWN REASON:
`aviFAIL` is one of the four knobs, so R11 already moves it to -1 from state
1 -- but that case then carries the open-loop arm AND the message branch at
once, and a defect in either is attributable to the other. State 2 holds
`StC_Mode` at 0, so the ONLY thing it runs is the copy loop and the message.
WHAT THESE STATES DO NOT REACH, stated here rather than left to the score:
the ErrMsg helpers' three remaining boundaries -- a supplied length of
exactly 1, a supplied length of 0 or less, and a message whose length equals
the staging capacity exactly. All three are properties of `ErrVar%ErrMsg`'s
LENGTH, and `_baseline_state` deliberately leaves every CHARACTER parameter
to R6's own ladder (`harness/generate.py:1107`), so no state in this file can
move them. They are declared in `mutation/StructuralControl.equivalences.json`
against a census, not excused.

states.name: open_loop_group_one_on_index_one
states.why: StC_Mode = 2 with StC_Group_N = 1 and Ind_StructControl(1) = 1 takes the open-loop arm at group 1 -- the only arm in this unit that calls interp1d and the only reader of the two OL_ arrays. OL_Breakpoints ramps 0, 1, 2, ... strictly increasing so interp1d raises no error; Time = 1.5 sits between two breakpoints so the interior arm runs and every gathered element can reach the answer. OL_StructControl ramps with a step, so a row gathered from the wrong stride or one element short gives a different interpolant. StC_Input starts at a ramp too, so the copy to avrSWAP is observable and so is the overwrite the arm performs on element 1.

states.name: error_message_with_no_arm_running
states.why: aviFAIL = -1 with StC_Mode = 0 enters the RoutineName prefix and nothing else: neither the step arm nor the open-loop arm runs, so a difference here is attributable to the message and to the copy loop alone. StC_Group_N = 1 keeps the copy loop alive so the state is not a no-op, and the ramps keep its two arrays distinct. The supplied ErrMsg is left to R6's character ladder, which is the one quantity this file cannot state.
